content:
maria: heads-up euc1 serving pool is hitting sustained 95% util and we're seeing 429s from the frontend. autoscaler didn't add new nodes for ~8m :eyes:

kai: on it, what pool? gpu-inference-euc1?

maria: yes. requests queued, new pods stuck in Pending with message `0/16 nodes are available`

provisioner-bot: [alert] failed to provision instance (zone=euc1-b) error=QUOTA_EXCEEDED, attempt=1

ashley: infra dashboards show provisioner heartbeats dropping around the same time. heartbeat: 0/5 for provisioner processes in euc1.

jonathan: autoscaler logs show scale decision computed but no inventory available. scale_reason="target_util>threshold" desired=+4, applied=0

maria: so autoscaler wanted to scale but cloud failed to provision due to quota. can we failover traffic?

kai: yes, we should shift weight off euc1 immediately. executing weighted shift to us-west-1 (30%) and us-east-1 (20%) to relieve queue. doing gradual 10% steps. ping @ashley for LB edits

ashley: applying shift now via control-plane. command: 
```
POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/traffic/shift
{ "from": "euc1", "to": ["us-west-1","us-east-1"], "weights": [0.6,0.3,0.1] }
```

ops-bot: [run] traffic shift started: euc1->us-west-1 (10%), us-east-1 (10%)

maria: 429s dropping to ~10% now, pending pods still queued though. we need quota fix or capacity reserve.

kai: I checked provisioner logs: noisy cloud API errors + preemptible shortage. Looks like recent deploy increased preemptible demand. provisioner retried but backoff hit limit.

jonathan: can we change autoscaler policy to allow fallback to non-preemptible pool? temp patch: set nodeSelector toleration to allow standard-gpu pool.

kai: doing a quick patch to the fleet-override. command: 
```
kubectl -n infra patch nodepool autoscaler-gpu --patch '{"spec": {"fallbackPools": ["standard-gpu-euc1"]}}'
```

provisioner-bot: [info] fallbackPools applied, attempting provisioning in standard-gpu-euc1

maria: also seeing thrash from the CPU-based metric — traffic is bursty but auth-proxy metrics spike and decay fast. we should smooth the metric window from 30s -> 120s to avoid overreacting.

jonathan: agree. updating autoscaler config to use 2m aggregation and increase scale-up cooldown to 90s to avoid oscillation. patch: 
```
PATCH /api/v1/autoscaler/config
{ "agg_window": 120, "scale_up_cooldown_sec": 90 }
```

ashley: change applied. monitoring for thrash.

maria: external: opened ticket with cloud to request temporary GPU quota bump in euc1 (case #CG-112233). they responded ETA ~2h. we can't wait.

kai: we have a small manual reserve we can bump in control-plane to handle emergencies. applying +3 nodes to reserve now.

ops-bot: [action] reserved_capacity increased: pool=gpu-inference-euc1 delta=+3 by kai

maria: pending pods went through after reserve increase. 429s are back to baseline. nice work.

jonathan: postmortem action items: 
- add fallback to non-preemptible pools in autoscaler policy by default
- expose quota short-circuit in console to request emergency bump faster
- add metric smoothing and longer cooldown to default policy for bursty workloads
- update runbook with traffic-shift steps and control-plane API example

kai: I'll own the autoscaler default policy change.

ashley: I'll add the runbook section and the console quick-request ticket flow.

maria: filing an incident note and tagging CS/ops teams. thanks everyone. :heart:

ops-bot: [incident-note] created incident IN-2026-97 summary="euc1 autoscale blocked by quota + provisioner heartbeat drop, temporary weighted traffic shift and reserve applied"

maria: closing thread once the runbook PR is merged and the cloud quota ticket resolves.

jonathan: added a short snippet to ops-runbook repo: 
```
# emergency weighted shift
curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/traffic/shift" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"from":"euc1","to":["us-west-1"],"weights":[0.8,0.2]}'
```

kai: thanks. we should also add alert that ties provisioner heartbeat drop -> auto open incident so it's not human dependent.

maria: agreed. creating follow-up ticket for automated incident firing.

ashley: nice quick response, everything stable now. :thumbsup:
